messages:
Leo H: SOS  had to go to an ER in Lisbon last night for a bad ankle sprain. Hospital wants payment up front and says our insurer won't do direct billing for international emergency care. I only have a digital copy of my card and the provider wants a printed copy. I leave tomorrow morningI don't have time to wait for carrier processing. Any way People Ops can help with direct bill or immediate proof?

Mira (People Ops): Sorry that happened, Leo. Two options: (A) get an employer-signed emergency coverage letter you can show at billing to avoid immediate cash demand (many hospitals accept it for emergency stabilization), or (B) pay OOP and we help submit a fast-track reimbursement claim with the carrier. Do you have the hospital name, date/time of service, your member ID, and the itemized bill/estimate?

Leo H: Member ID: L004332110. Hospital: Hospital CUF Porto. Service: ER visit + ankle x-ray on 2026-09-14 at 23:40. They gave an estimate of 950 EUR and are asking for 300 EUR now to release me. I have a photo of the estimate and a scanned copy of my digital card. Passport with me.

Omar - Benefits: For true emergencies carriers will usually reimburse, but direct billing policies differ by network and country. We can: 1) issue a company-signed Emergency Proof of Coverage letter listing member ID, policy name, and statement that this is for emergency stabilization while the carrier processes international claims; 2) contact the carrier's international assistance desk (Global Assist) to request a provider-side pre-auth/direct-bill or guarantee of payment; 3) prepare the claim forms (UB-04 or itemized invoice) for quick upload. If you prefer not to pay, present the employer letter + passport and ask them to accept a deposit; many hospitals will accept an ID + guarantor letter for a reduced deposit.

BenefitsBot: \u2705 Ticket created: #BEN-5300 \u2014 "International ER - direct bill / urgent reimbursement". Assigned to Omar. Target response: 4 hours for initial outreach to carrier and same-day employer letter generation. Please upload itemized bill and photos to BEN-5300 or email benefits@redwood.com with subject EXACT: "INTL ER - Leo H - URGENT".

Leo H: I emailed benefits@redwood.com with subject EXACT: "INTL ER - Leo H - URGENT" and attached the hospital estimate + digital card screenshot + passport photo. They insist on a local ID and printed card. Do you have a letter template I can print and hand them now?

Mira (People Ops): Yes. Here's the exact text we'll produce (you can copy/print while we finalize the signed PDF):

"To whom it may concern,

This letter confirms that Leo Hernandez (DOB 1991-02-18), member ID L004332110, is an active participant in Redwood Inference medical plan. This document is provided as emergency proof of coverage and employer guarantor for the purpose of emergency stabilization care on 14 September 2026 at Hospital CUF Porto. Redwood has initiated an urgent request with the carrier for direct billing and/or expedited reimbursement. Please accept this letter and the patient's passport as temporary verification of coverage pending carrier confirmation.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Benefits Team
Contact: benefits@redwood.com
"

Omar - Benefits: Confirmed receipt of your email and attachments. I'm calling Global Assist now to request a provider guarantee of payment and to confirm how the hospital can submit direct-bill documents. If carrier declines direct billing, we'll instruct you on paying the minimum deposit and we'll fast-track the reimbursement. Keep all receipts and get an itemized invoice in English if possible.

Clinic Intl Billing: We received a call from Redwood Benefits regarding Leo H. If you present a signed employer letter and passport, our international desk can reduce the upfront deposit. We will need the member ID and date of service and then submit the claim to the carrier. If the carrier refuses guarantee, we can accept a deposit and issue an itemized invoice for reimbursement. We can send an English invoice via email upon request.

Leo H: I printed the copied text and showed it to admissions. They allowed me to be seen and accepted a 150 EUR deposit after the manager called the billing desk. They said they'll email an itemized invoice in English. Thank you!! What do I do next to get reimbursed fast?

Omar - Benefits: Great. Next steps: 1) Upload the final itemized invoice (PDF) and proof of payment (receipt showing 150 EUR) to the BEN-5300 ticket or email benefits@redwood.com. 2) Fill out the carrier's international claim form if included in the invoice packet (we can fill on your behalf if you forward it). 3) We'll send the claim with a cover letter requesting expedited processing due to emergency care while traveling. If you paid OOP, expect initial carrier reimbursement window of 7-14 business days once they accept the claim; we'll follow up with provider relations to try to speed that to 3-7 business days. We'll also request cash advance subrogation if the carrier delays.

BenefitsBot: Ticket BEN-5300 updated: carrier outreach initiated; employer emergency letter generated and uploaded. Please confirm when you upload the final invoice and receipt.

Leo H: Uploading invoice and receipt now. Also flag: will this affect my out-of-pocket maximums in the US plan?

Omar - Benefits: Yes, reimbursed amounts count toward your in-network/out-of-network OOP depending on how the carrier processes the claim. We'll request the carrier to apply emergency out-of-network protections per plan terms. If there's a shortfall after reimbursement, we'll review appeals and potential plan-level exceptions. Keep all correspondence.

Mira (People Ops): If anything goes sideways in the airport or with follow-up billing, DM me and we'll escalate to the benefits manager. Hope you heal fast let us know if you need local care referrals or transport assistance. :+1:
